name: Laguna de los Tres, under Fitz Roy
region: Los Glaciares National Park, north sector
why: The classic Patagonian day: forest, two lakes and, after a brutal last hour, Fitz Roy's granite straight above a glacier lake.
book: Free, no permit. Read the trail status at the national park visitor centre the day before.
water: Streams are drinkable along the way; nothing to buy after the village.
dangers: The last kilometre climbs 400 m on loose rock: slow, steep and exposed to the wind.
Gusts over 80 km/h are common on the top: stay back from the edge.
Snow on the last climb until late November.
turnaround: If you reach Campamento Poincenot after 13:00, stop at the river: the climb and the way back take 5 more hours.

points.name: Fitz Roy trailhead, El Chaltén
points.note: At the north end of Avenida San Martín, by the park sign. The first hour climbs above the Río de las Vueltas.

points.name: Mirador del Fitz Roy
points.note: First full view of the massif, after about 4 km. On a cloudy morning this may be all you see: decide here.

points.name: Laguna Capri
points.note: A short detour to the lake; its camp is the quiet alternative to Poincenot.

points.name: Campamento Poincenot
points.note: Last flat ground, toilets and water. Leave anything heavy here; the climb starts across the Río Blanco bridge.

points.name: Laguna de los Tres
points.note: 1,170 m. Walk 5 minutes to the left for Laguna Sucia far below.
